newsitem.title: USA: Canada energy firms see continued merger frenzy.
newsitem.headline: Canada energy firms see continued merger frenzy.

text.p: A mergers and acquisitions feeding frenzy among Canadian oil and natural gas producers is set to continue because new land leases are so expensive, company executives told a conference here on Thurday.
"We are always ready for a good opportunity but it has to be a strong fit," David Johnson, chief executive of Encal Energy Ltd told a conference organized by Canadian broker FirstEnergy.
In Saskatchewan in August 1996, a then-record price of C$24,859 per hectare was paid for a lease, compared with the previous record of C$17,038 a year earlier.

Amber Energy Inc, which expects to double its oil output this year with the inclusion of the Pelican Lake field in Alberta, said it too intends to keep an eye on potential bid targets. "We are ready to continue to expand," chief financial officer James Lough told the conference.
Canadian Natural Resources Ltd, which this week set up a C$300 million medium term note program, is also in the market.

The Canadian energy sector saw strong levels of M&A activity in 1996, and 1997 has started off with Gulf Canada Resources Ltd winning control of Britain's Clyde Petroleum Plc, a C$1.7 billion bid for Wascana Energy Inc from Talisman Energy Inc, an agreed offer for Cimarron Petroleum Ltd from Newport Petroleum Corp and a friendly bid for Northstar Energy Corp from Morrison Petroleums Ltd.
Low interest rates and high oil and gas prices are some reasons driving the M&A spree, but the rising price of extraction rights sold by Canada is playing its part.
"We have a lots of room to move if the right opportunity presents itself," said company chairman John Langille.

The company is forecasting that its debt to equity ratio will rise to C$732 million in 1997 from C$580 million in 1996 and that its debt to cashflow multiple will fall to 1.3 times from 1.6 times as cashflow grows to C$550 million from C$360 million. ((-- David Chance New York Newsroom 212 859 1902))
